Start group-kill test timeout once its child is ready (TODO 253) (#282)

1 run of tools/test-skill-release-date-client.py errored with
FileNotFoundError for sleeper.pid in
test_a_child_that_does_not_end_is_killed_with_its_group; 3 reruns
passed, and a rerun that passes does not clear a failure.

The 1 second timeout started before the stub child had forked its
sleeper and written sleeper.pid, so a slow start let the group kill
land before the pid file existed. Host load is the inferred cause of
the slow start: the log records no load, and a 2 second delay before
the pid write reproduces the error.

The sleeper, its pid file and the probe of its pid with os.kill are
removed. The stub child now forks 1 member into its group and then
writes 1 byte to a FIFO, alive, and the client's first wait starts
only once the test reads that byte, polled for at most 60 seconds, as
in the capped-child test beside it; the poll is new to this test. The
test asserts the client's reason first, then that the byte was read
when the poll ended, that the client asked its first wait for exactly
its 1 second timeout, that the real wait lasted at least that long,
and that the client's run, less the poll, ended within 15 seconds;
main bounded the whole run by 15 seconds.

End of file on alive within 10 seconds after the client returns shows
that the client killed the whole group, not only the leader: it comes
only once every process holding the write end has ended. Each stub
process otherwise ends by itself 90 seconds after it enters its wait
for the release, and so more than 90 seconds after the test's start.
The check takes no end of file after 85 seconds from that start, the
60 second poll, the 15 second run and the 10 second check, plus the
poll's last step, and end of file must come before 90 seconds, so the
group's own end is never taken for the kill.

The test sends no signal. Each stub process waits for end of file on
a second FIFO, lifeline, whose only write end the test holds, and
ignores SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP. The check's finally clause closes
lifeline and reaps a child the client left unreaped, and the kernel
closes lifeline when the test process ends in any other way. The stub
reads lifeline once before it forks, a read the planned design did not
have: a FIFO reader opened with no writer sees no end of file, so a
stub that starts after the release would otherwise wait out its 90
seconds; with the read it exits at once. A stub process past that read
ends at once on the release; one not yet there ends when it reaches
it, after the rest of its start-up, which the test does not bound.

The check writes own_end into the stub's source and adds check and
own_end to clock readings, so it admits as each only a value whose
type is exactly int or float and raises TypeError for any other, a
subclass included: a caller's value can then add no code to the stub
and run none of its own through an operator.

New tests run the check against a client that kills only the leader,
one that sends SIGTERM to the group, a stub whose own end falls inside
the check, and a client whose group kill raises KeyboardInterrupt, and
assert that each fails or passes the interrupt through and that the
group ends within 5 seconds after it. They also assert that a stub
started after the release exits at once, that an own_end or check
whose methods run code raises TypeError without running it, and that
every callee of the check and its helpers is on a fixed list, the
calls that start a process are pinned with their arguments, the type
test is the check's first statement and those 2 names are not rebound,
the stub's calls are pinned in order, and no signal-sending name
appears in any of them. That last test compares names only, so a
signal function reached as a value without its name passes it. The
group-kill test asserts nothing about the client's reap; its docstring
names the 2 tests that do.

Residual: a stub process that the release finds before its first read
of lifeline outlives the release by the rest of its start-up. While
the test process is alive but neither closes lifeline nor ends, as
when it is stopped, each stub process lives its start-up plus 90
seconds. The syntax-tree check does not read the client or the
standard library, and does not cover values a caller supplies other
than check and own_end, such as the witness it passes or a module
global it rebinds. A client whose real wait gives up early by less
than the time the gate's 2 clock reads and the call add passes; the
call's share includes the wait's overrun past its own deadline, which
the code does not bound, so the host sets the margin. A process that
SIGKILL cannot end keeps alive open and fails the check. A correct
client still fails if the child is not ready within 60 seconds. The
design needs FIFOs and select on them, and was run only on Linux with
Python 3.14.

Unchanged from main: the 1 second timeout, the reason string, the
real wait, kill and reap, and a 10 second window for the group to end
after the client returns. With a 2 second delay before the pid write,
main's test fails. A client that kills only the group leader, one
that never kills, one whose first wait asks for half its timeout and
one whose real wait gives up at half its timeout each fail the new
test.

The client's run_extractor catches Exception broadly and leaves its
child's group running when KeyboardInterrupt passes through it; that
is left for a later item.

  the Pull request text gate.
